best_architecture: Recommended pattern for Local-Claw is a MemGPT/Letta-inspired tiered (OS-virtual-memory) architecture layered on top of the existing MongoDB + Chroma + Redis stack, organized by memory FUNCTION (cognitive tiers) rather than by storage engine. Three function tiers map cleanly onto the three datastores. (1) Core / working memory (the LLM's RAM): a small, always-in-context block holding the agent persona, current task/goal, the active file/repo summary, and a self-editable scratchpad of recent salient facts. Keep this in Redis (fast key-value, per-session) and inject it verbatim into every prompt. Budget it as a hard token cap (e.g. ~2-4k tokens of a ~8-32k window) so the rest of the window is free for retrieved evidence and reasoning. (2) Recall memory (disk cache): the raw, searchable conversation/turn + tool-call history. Store full transcripts and tool I/O in MongoDB (sessions/docs collections) with timestamps and metadata; index the searchable text in Chroma so the agent can semantically search its own history via a tool. (3) Archival memory (cold storage / long-term knowledge): processed, de-contextualized knowledge - code patterns, API/library facts, project conventions, learned skills - embedded into Chroma for vector retrieval, with the canonical records persisted in MongoDB. Crucially, separate the three COGNITIVE memory types per the CoALA taxonomy across these tiers: EPISODIC ('what happened' - specific past sessions, bug fixes, tool traces) lives in recall+archival with recency/relevance/salience-weighted retrieval (Generative Agents scoring); SEMANTIC ('what is true' - project facts, library docs, user preferences, conventions) is extracted and consolidated into archival memory; PROCEDURAL ('how to do it' - verified, reusable code snippets/skills indexed by NL description, the Voyager skill-library pattern) is the highest-value tier for a CODING agent and should be a dedicated, curated Chroma collection of validated skills the agent can compose. Key design decisions, in order of importance: (a) Self-editing vs passive extraction - give the agent explicit memory tools (core_memory_append, archival_memory_insert, archival_memory_search, recall_search) so it curates its own memory during the reasoning loop (Letta model); supplement with an automatic background extraction/consolidation pass (mem0 ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP model) so nothing critical is lost if the model forgets to save. Use mem0's conflict-resolution (don't append duplicate facts; update/delete superseded ones) to keep memory lean. (b) Context-window budgeting - enforce explicit token budgets per tier and a self-managed 'memory pressure' trigger: when the recent-turn buffer approaches the budget, summarize older turns into a recursive summary (MemGPT's queue/flush mechanism), write the raw turns to recall (Mongo), and keep only the summary in core. (c) Retrieval scoring - rank archival/episodic hits by a weighted blend of recency + semantic relevance + importance/salience rather than pure cosine similarity. (d) Consolidation/forgetting - run a periodic (or memory-pressure-triggered) consolidation job that promotes repeated episodic observations into semantic facts, merges near-duplicates, applies confidence decay, and summarizes; use Redis queues to schedule these background jobs. (e) Single retrieval interface - expose memory to Gemma/Qwen as a small fixed set of MCP tools so the same interface works regardless of which model is driving. Net: tiered virtual-context manager (Letta/MemGPT) + automatic fact extraction & conflict resolution (mem0) + recency/relevance/importance retrieval (Generative Agents) + an explicit procedural skill library (Voyager), persisted as Redis=working, MongoDB=durable record, Chroma=vector index.
reference_papers: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems (Packer et al. 2023) - arxiv:2310.08560 - foundational tiered virtual-context-management model (core/recall/archival memory, OS-inspired paging, self-editing memory functions, memory-pressure summarization); basis of Letta.

Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior (Park et al. 2023) - arxiv:2304.03442 - memory stream with recency + relevance + importance(salience) retrieval scoring and reflection/consolidation; the canonical retrieval-ranking design.

Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents / CoALA (Sumers, Yao, Narasimhan, Griffiths 2023) - arxiv:2309.02427 - taxonomy distinguishing working, episodic, semantic, and procedural memory for language agents; the conceptual framework for tiering coding-agent memory.

Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models (Wang et al. 2023) - arxiv:2305.16291 - skill library = procedural memory: verified executable skills indexed by natural-language description and composed for new tasks; directly applicable to a coding agent's reusable-code-pattern store.

Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory (Chhikara et al. 2025) - arxiv:2504.19413 - extraction + ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP conflict-resolution memory layer; reports ~26k->~1.7k token reduction vs full-context and p95 ~0.2s retrieval on LOCOMO.

Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory (Rasmussen et al. 2025) - arxiv:2501.13956 - temporal knowledge graph (Graphiti engine) tracking how facts change over time; reports strong LongMemEval results (temporal/relational reasoning). [uncertain] exact arxiv id

Position: Episodic Memory is the Missing Piece for Long-Term LLM Agents (2025) - arxiv:2502.06975 - argues episodic memory (instance-specific, context-preserved experience) is the key gap for long-horizon agents.

Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Emerging Frontiers (2025/2026) - arxiv:2603.07670 - survey of agent memory mechanisms, tiers, and evaluation. [uncertain] arxiv id/date may be a preprint placeholder
reference_repos: letta-ai/letta (formerly cpacker/MemGPT) - open-source stateful-agent framework implementing the MemGPT core/recall/archival tiers with self-editing memory, automatic persistence, and pluggable vector/DB backends - https://github.com/letta-ai/letta

mem0ai/mem0 - most-adopted standalone memory layer (~48k stars); automatic fact extraction with ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP conflict resolution; 20+ vector backends including Chroma and Redis; works with any LLM/orchestrator - https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0

getzep/zep + getzep/graphiti - temporal-knowledge-graph memory server (Graphiti is the underlying temporal KG engine) for tracking evolving facts/relationships over time - https://github.com/getzep/zep , https://github.com/getzep/graphiti

elizaOS/agentmemory - lightweight pip-installable agent memory powered by chromadb and postgres; simple episodic/semantic API, DBScan memory clustering, distance-threshold + novelty filtering; closest match to the 'agentmemory' library and easy to slot onto Chroma - https://github.com/elizaOS/agentmemory

NirDiamant/Agent_Memory_Techniques - 30 runnable notebooks covering buffers, vector stores, knowledge graphs, episodic/semantic memory, MemGPT, Mem0, Letta, Zep, Graphiti, and LOCOMO/LongMemEval patterns; best reference implementation catalog - https://github.com/NirDiamant/Agent_Memory_Techniques

langchain-ai/langmem - LangGraph-native long-term memory utilities (semantic/episodic/procedural memory management, background consolidation) for agents already in the LangChain ecosystem - https://github.com/langchain-ai/langmem [uncertain] exact repo path

redis/agent-memory-server (Redis Agent Memory Server) - low-latency Redis-backed working + long-term memory service with REST/MCP interface; useful as the working-memory tier - https://github.com/redis/agent-memory-server [uncertain] exact repo path/owner
key_libraries: mem0ai (mem0) - Python (also TS/JS) - pip install mem0ai, ~v0.1.117+ (Sept 2025) - automatic memory extraction, conflict resolution, and retrieval; native Chroma and Redis vector backends plus MongoDB support; primary recommended memory layer for Local-Claw.

letta / letta-client - Python - pip install letta (server) + letta-client - MemGPT tiered-memory agent runtime with self-editing core/recall/archival memory and pluggable Postgres/pgvector + embedding backends; use for the tiered virtual-context manager and memory-tool interface.

chromadb - Python - pip install chromadb (~v0.5/0.6+, 2025) - the vector store for recall (transcript) and archival/procedural (knowledge + skill) embeddings; already in the Local-Claw stack; backs elizaOS/agentmemory and mem0.

agentmemory (elizaOS) - Python - pip install agentmemory - thin ChromaDB+Postgres wrapper with create/search/update/delete-memory, clustering, and novelty filtering; quick way to get episodic/semantic stores on top of existing Chroma.

redis-py + redisvl (Redis Vector Library) - Python - pip install redis redisvl - working-memory tier (per-session core memory, caches) and background consolidation/job queues; redisvl adds vector search if a Redis-backed recall index is wanted.
pymongo / motor - Python - durable session + document store for raw transcripts, tool traces, and canonical memory records (the recall/archival system of record behind the Chroma index).

sentence-transformers OR a local embedding model (e.g. bge / nomic-embed / e5) - Python - pip install sentence-transformers - on-box embeddings for archival/recall vectors, keeping retrieval local on the RTX A6000 (no external embedding API).

graphiti-core (Zep) - Python - pip install graphiti-core - optional temporal-knowledge-graph layer if Local-Claw needs to track how project facts/relationships evolve over time; heavier than vector-only memory.
langmem - Python - pip install langmem - optional if adopting LangGraph; provides semantic/episodic/procedural memory managers and background consolidation. [uncertain] package name/version
